clusters.name: Gordon's death, 1991–1992
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon's death in June 1991, within months: your wrist injury stopped your playing that autumn, a blow-up with Rafe followed, you were on your own getting high and absorbed in fixing radios, and by early 1992 you were lost and low, unable to get going. The shift in functioning is tied to grief and the loss of footing after his death and the injury together.

clusters.name: Winifred's cancer diagnosis, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around the time your grandmother Winifred was found to have bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002, within months: you were running out of steam for performing and anxious, you had a disastrous audition and were done with it, you grew distant from family and friends, you left Thornbury for Gull Harbour, met Marisol and moved to Fenwick with her, and when that split up within the year you sank into a deep depression. You returned to Thornbury unable to face your family and relied on friends instead; the shifts pile up through your separation and the months after, settling as you began to move toward help.

clusters.name: Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within months: you were too drained for conversation with your mother at Alder Creek in July, she pressed you to visit and you kept the door shut on her, and when you left for nursing school in August you stopped speaking to her altogether. The silence held for roughly a year; your distance from her is the core shift around her death and the months after.

clusters.name: Frances's retirement party, 2019
clusters.reason: Around Frances's retirement party at the lake house in October 2019: Wren was swamped one thing after another, you moved into overfunctioning to settle her, her family talks all day with nothing happening to one that the others don't hear, and at the lake weekend you were awake from the small hours with no more sleep and could only pull back as the others rose. Wren grew anxious when you'd had no sleep at family occasions and the drive home was long and quiet. The shifts are yours and Wren's, tangled together through the weekend around her family gathering.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
